messages.author: 51af56f8dba6ef19
messages.subject: boxplot strange behavior
parts:
Hello,

I generate box plots from my data like this:

qplot(x=xxx,y=column,data=data,geom="boxplot") + xlab("xxx") + ylab(ylabel) + theme_bw() + scale_y_log10() + geom_jitter(alpha=I(1/10))

The problem is that I see lot of points below the minimum at the same level as some outliers. I looks very weird as I expected the outliers to be "few" and specially not see any points other than the outliers below the minimum or above the maximum. 

Can anyone explain what's going on?

Attached I send a snapshot, see the second level having some outliers above but separate from the outliers there are also points which seem not to be outliers and that are outside the maximum indicator? is this a bug or am I missing anything?

TIA,
Best regards,
Giovanni

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: boxplot strange behavior
parts:
What you're seeing is the effect of jittering - the outside points (in black) extend from the whiskers, the grey points are the same set of points jittered. If you don't want that effect, then either don't jitter or suppress the outside points inside the geom_boxplot() call; see the outlier options under 'Parameters' in the on-line help page for geom_boxplot:

http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_boxplot.html

Dennis

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: boxplot strange behavior
parts:
It might be less confusing if you use ggplot instead of qplot, and also use geom_point instead of geom_jitter. The equivalent would probably look something like this:

ggplot(data, aes(x=xxx, y=column)) + geom_boxplot() +
    geom_point(position="jitter")

I think the issue is that you're jittering the points from geom_point, but not the outlier points from geom_boxplot. I don't think it's possible to jitter the outlier points from the boxplot geom.

You should be able to change the outlier size and shape to help deal with the overplotting, with something like this:
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 21, outlier.size = 1)
This will make smaller points and use hollow circles. I think you may need the development version for this, though.

-Winston

messages.author: 92a06be4d96a96ee
messages.subject: Re: boxplot strange behavior
parts:
The native geom_boxplot doesn't support it, but once upon a time I found a post with revised version for jitter and I added alpha also.

GeomBoxplotJitterOutlier <- proto(GeomBoxplot, {
   draw <- function (., data, ..., outlier.colour = "black", outlier.shape = 16, 
    outlier.size = 2, outlier.jitter=0,outlier.alpha=1) {
# copy the body of function 'draw' above and paste here.
defaults <- with(data, data.frame(x = x, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, 
        colour = colour, size = size, linetype = 1, group = 1, 
        alpha = 1, fill = alpha(fill, alpha), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    defaults2 <- defaults[c(1, 1), ]
        if (!is.null(data$outliers) && length(data$outliers[[1]] >= 
        1)) {
            pp<-position_jitter(width=outlier.jitter,height=0)
            p<-pp$adjust(data.frame(x=data$x[rep(1, length(data$outliers[[1]]))], y=data$outliers[[1]]),.scale)
        outliers_grob <- GeomPoint$draw(data.frame(x=p$x, y = p$y, colour = I(outlier.colour), 
            shape = outlier.shape, alpha = outlier.alpha, size = outlier.size, 
            fill = NA), ...)
    }
    else {
        outliers_grob <- NULL
    }
    with(data, ggname(.$my_name(), grobTree(outliers_grob, GeomPath$draw(data.frame(y = c(upper, 
        ymax), defaults2), ...), GeomPath$draw(data.frame(y = c(lower, 
        ymin), defaults2), ...), GeomRect$draw(data.frame(ymax = upper, 
        ymin = lower, defaults), ...), GeomRect$draw(data.frame(ymax = middle, 
        ymin = middle, defaults), ...))))

}

  objname <- "boxplot_jitter_outlier"
  desc <- "Box and whiskers plot with jittered outlier"
  guide_geom <- function(.) "boxplot_jitter_outlier"

})
geom_boxplot_jitter_outlier <- GeomBoxplotJitterOutlier$build_accessor()

#example plot call
#  ggplot(test, aes(x=places,y=value))+geom_boxplot_jitter_outlier(outlier.jitter=0.05)


Hope that helps,

Justin
